title: 'We are sorry': Rocks found in restaurant burritos in Alberta
summary: BarBurrito issued an apology to its customers after pea-sized stones were found in some of its burritos at restaurants in Alberta. The company says the rocks came from a particular brand of beans…

image.caption: A small rock found inside a burrito purchased Nov. 2 from BarBurrito in southeast Calgary. The company has apologized for rocks found in its food, saying they've linked them to a particular brand of beans from its food supplier. (Saskia McNeill)

blocks.text: Calgary

BarBurrito issued an apology to its customers after pea-sized stones were found in some of its burritos at restaurants in Alberta. The company says the rocks came from a particular brand of beans that it is no longer using.
BarBurrito switching bean supplier after at least 3 incidents where small rocks found in food

A Calgary woman who found a pea-sized rock in her burrito is pleased to see an apology from the company, but questions why it took BarBurrito 17 days to respond to her complaints and issue a public notice.
Saskia McNeill, her husband and their six-year-old son ordered home delivery Nov. 2 from BarBurrito, a Canadian restaurant chain with hundreds of locations across the country.
After five or six bites into her burrito, she chomped down on something that didn't feel right.
“I just felt something like, very hard. And then I just took it out and discovered it was a stone basically the size of a pea,” McNeil said from her home in southeast Calgary.
She doesn't think any of her teeth were damaged, but she quickly put an end to dinner time. She told her family to stop eating and then called the restaurant multiple times without getting through.
Saskia McNeill retrieves a small rock she found inside a burrito purchased from BarBurrito in Calgary. (Bryan Labby/CBC)
The family then drove to the strip mall in the community of Legacy where the restaurant is located, and spoke to an employee she described as sympathetic.
"He took a picture of the stone. He was very friendly. He was very understanding and he took our number and he reassured that the manager was going to give us a call."
She says that didn't happen.
A week later, with frustration mounting, McNeill posted an online review of the restaurant and was stunned to see someone else had found a rock in their burrito.
A review posted by someone who found a rock inside their burrito purchased at BarBurrito in southeast Calgary. (Google Reviews)
McNeill says it was upsetting to see the second stone show up after she warned the restaurant about her discovery.
“All I wanted was this location to take safety seriously," she said.
A third rock was found inside a burrito purchased at BarBurrito in Canmore, Alta.
The partner of a CBC journalist said he found this rock in a burrito he bought in Canmore in September.
A small stone found in a burrito purchased at BarBurrito in Canmore, Alta. (Submitted by Aaron Wright)
McNeill says after she saw the second stone review she contacted Alberta Health Services' environmental public health branch to report the incident.
She shared her experience and photos with a food inspector, who visited and inspected the restaurant, according to AHS.

AHS said in an email that "to date EPH has received one complaint of this nature." It provided no other information related to the investigation, but did say it takes all complaints seriously and follows up on concerns brought to its attention.
Manager, company apologize
McNeill says the inspector told her he visited the restaurant this week and on Wednesday the store manager contacted her.
“She was very respectful. She apologized so many times."
CBC News reached out to the company on Thursday and within hours it posted a message on its website apologizing for the unwanted ingredients in its food.
"Some of our guests have found small stones in beans served at our restaurants in Calgary and Canmore. We are sorry. That should never happen in food we serve."
The company says other locations in Western Canada may have been affected as well.
In an email to the CBC, the company said the "source of the rocks" has been linked to a particular brand of beans the company purchases from a food distributor in Western Canada.
A notice to customers inside the BarBurrito in southeast Calgary on Nov. 19, 2026. (Bryan Labby/CBC)

"As a result, we have removed all beans from this supplier across all affected locations. We’re actively procuring beans from alternative suppliers which currently supply our Eastern Canada locations."
It says all locations remain open and once the bean supply has been restored, the company says it will add extra inspections before the beans are prepared.
McNeill says she doesn't understand why the company took so long to respond to her complaints and suggests inquiries from CBC News may have expedited the response.
“It was just the non-communication, the not responding, that's what I don't understand.”
She says she turned down refund and gift card offers from the company.
"It's not about getting a free meal. It's about the safety. And all we wanted from you guys is to let us know you're taking care of that."
